title: Crisp Bubble and Squeak with Savoy Cabbage
summary: Buttery mashed potato folded with onion and savoy cabbage, pressed into a non-stick pan and fried in butter until deeply browned and crisp on both sides.
equipment: 30 cm non-stick frying pan with lid

ingredients.item: floury potatoes, peeled and sliced 6 mm thick
fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water
savoy cabbage (about half a small head), cored and cut into 2.5 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the potatoes with water in the saucepan, add 2 tsp salt and bring to the boil. Simmer for 8-10 min until a knife meets no resistance. Drain, return to the pan, add 40 g butter and the pepper and mash until smooth.

steps.title: Cook the cabbage
steps.text: Melt 15 g butter in the frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for about 4 min until soft. Add the cabbage, water and 1/2 tsp salt, cover and cook for about 10 min, stirring once, until wilted and tender. Fold the cabbage into the potatoes and wipe out the pan.

steps.title: Brown the first side
steps.text: Melt 20 g butter in the pan over medium heat. Pack in the potato mixture and press it into an even cake with the spatula. Cook without stirring for 6-8 min until a deep golden crust forms underneath. Leaving it alone is what builds the crust.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Slide the cake onto the plate, invert the pan over it and turn both over together. Add the remaining 20 g butter around the edge and cook for 6-8 min more, until the second side is crisp and the cake is hot through. Cut into wedges and serve.

tips: Floury potatoes such as Maris Piper or King Edward give the fluffiest mash and the best crust.
Leftover cooked potatoes, cabbage, sprouts or carrots work just as well.
Top each wedge with a fried egg for brunch, cooked until the yolk is set.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Refrigerate the mixture or leftover wedges up to 2 days. Re-fry in a little butter until crisp and piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
